title: ENGINE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the procedure for disconnecting the engine from the engine mount prior to removal from the firewall?
answer: Remove the Engine and the Engine Mount. NOTE:  This procedure shows how you remove the engine and engine mount from the firewall. If the engine is removed from the engine mount and the engine mount stays attached to the firewall, some of the steps will not be necessary. To disconnect the engine from the engine mount, remove the (4) AN7 bolts that connect the (4) shock mounts to the engine mounting flange and the engine mount tube. (1) Set all cabin switches to the OFF position. (2)  Set the fuel shutoff valve to the OFF position. (3) Remove the engine cowl. Refer to Chapter 71, Cowling - Maintenance Practices. NOTE:  Do the subsequent steps from the right side of the airplane. (4)  Disconnect the positive and negative battery leads from the battery. (5) Loosen the C-clamp that attaches the flexible duct to the firewall-mounted heater valve. (6)  Remove the flexible duct from the heater valve. WARNING: If the P lead wire from the magnetos is disconnected, the electrical ground is removed from the magneto circuit. This will cause hot magnetos. Attach a ground wire to the magneto or remove all the high tension wires from the spark plugs before you turn the propeller. (7)  Disconnect the P lead wires on the magnetos. (8)  Remove the propeller governor.  Refer to Chapter 61, Propeller Governor - Maintenance Practices. (9)  Disconnect the electrical connector from the Exhaust Gas Temperature  Probe.  Disconnect the fuel outlet line at the fuel strainer. Disconnect the throttle cable at the fuel/air control unit and record the position of the washers and spacers for later installation.  Disconnect the vacuum hoses at the firewall-mounted manifold/check valve.  Disconnect and put a label on the electrical wires on the low vacuum annunciator switches. NOTE:  Do the subsequent steps from the left side of the airplane.  Loosen and remove the clamps from the tachometer drive cable in the engine area.  Disconnect the tachometer drive cable from the rear of the accessory case.  Cut the tie wraps  that attach the different wire bundles to the engine mount.  On the bottom side of the engine, loosen and remove the clamps that attach the starter wires to the sump area.  Remove the starter wires from the starter.  Disconnect the ground strap from the engine mount.  Disconnect the electrical connector from the fuel flow transducer.  Remove the two screws on the rear side of the upper right baffles. Remove the electrical connector from the baffles and separate the baffles.  Loosen the clamps that attach the battery vent tube to the drain line cluster.  Remove the vent tube through the clamps.  Remove the bolt and spacer that attach the drain line cluster to the firewall.  Loosen and remove the ram air tubes on the rear side of the upper left baffle.  Put a stand under the tail tie-down to adjust for a tail heavy condition, which will occur when the engine is removed from the airframe.  Attach the hoist to the lifting strap on top of the engine. CAUTION: Do not lift the engine higher than necessary. If you lift the engine too high, it puts a strain on the attach bolts.  Start to take up the engine weight using the hoist.  Remove the bolts that attach the engine and engine mount to the firewall. NOTE:  Record the sequence of nuts, washers, and flat washers. NOTE:  You can get access to the bolt heads from inside the cockpit to keep them from turning.  Slowly lift the engine using the hoist until the engine and engine mount move free of the bolts.

title: ENGINE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the specific procedures for connecting the various hoses, wires, and control cables during the engine installation process as described in the maintenance instructions?
answer: Install the Engine and Engine Mount. (1) Attach the engine mount to the firewall. Refer to Engine Mount - Maintenance Practices. (2) Lift the engine into position with the hoist. (3) Torque the firewall bolts to between 160 and 190 inch-pounds. (4) Remove the stand from under the tail tie-down. (5) Attach the ram air tubes to the rear side of the upper left baffle. (6) Attach the drain line cluster to the firewall with a bolt and spacer. (7) Put the battery vent tube through the drain line clamps and tighten the clamps. (8) Put the wires from the electrical connector through the baffle cutout area. (9)  Attach the baffle pieces together with screws.  Connect the electrical connector to the oil pressure transducer.  Connect the ground strap to the engine mount.  Connect the starter wires to the starter.  Connect the different wire bundles to the engine mount with tie wraps.  Connect the tachometer drive cable to the rear of the accessory case.  Connect the tagged wires to the low vacuum annunciator switches.  Connect the vacuum lines to the firewall-mounted manifold/check valve.  Connect the throttle and mixture control cables to the fuel air control unit.  Connect the fuel outlet line to the fuel strainer.  Connect the electrical connector to the EGT Probe.  Install the propeller governor. Refer to Chapter 61, Propeller Governor - Maintenance Practices.  Connect the P leads to the magnetos.  If necessary, connect the high tension wires to the spark plugs.  Connect the flexible duct to the firewall-mounted heater valve.  Make sure that all the controls and lines are installed correctly and can move freely.  Make sure that all fuel fittings are tight and that there are no leaks.  Connect the positive and negative leads to the battery.  Install the engine cowl. Refer to Chapter 71, Cowl - Maintenance Practices.

Disconnect the vacuum hoses at the firewall-mounted manifold/check valve.  Disconnect and put a label on the electrical wires on the low vacuum annunciator switches. NOTE:  Do the subsequent steps from the left side of the airplane.  Loosen and remove the clamps from the tachometer drive cable in the engine area.  Disconnect the tachometer drive cable from the rear of the accessory case.  Cut the tie wraps  that attach the different wire bundles to the engine mount.  On the bottom side of the engine, loosen and remove the clamps that attach the starter wires to the sump area.  Remove the starter wires from the starter.  Disconnect the ground strap from the engine mount.  Disconnect the electrical connector from the fuel flow transducer.  Remove the two screws on the rear side of the upper right baffles. Remove the electrical connector from the baffles and separate the baffles.  Loosen the clamps that attach the battery vent tube to the drain line cluster.  Remove the vent tube through the clamps.  Remove the bolt and spacer that attach the drain line cluster to the firewall.  Loosen and remove the ram air tubes on the rear side of the upper left baffle.  Put a stand under the tail tie-down to adjust for a tail heavy condition, which will occur when the engine is removed from the airframe.  Attach the hoist to the lifting strap on top of the engine. CAUTION: Do not lift the engine higher than necessary. If you lift the engine too high, it puts a strain on the attach bolts.  Start to take up the engine weight using the hoist.  Remove the bolts that attach the engine and engine mount to the firewall. NOTE:  Record the sequence of nuts, washers, and flat washers. NOTE:  You can get access to the bolt heads from inside the cockpit to keep them from turning.  Slowly lift the engine using the hoist until the engine and engine mount move free of the bolts.
